Incorporating Issue #10 RuntimeConfig capabilities into Issue #3 (DESIGN) **Status:** Proposed Issue #3 requirements only. The working Issue #10 implementation remains the source of behavior. At this revision, Issue #3 accepts only \`runOn="$"\` and \`runOn="gh"\`; it does **not** accept the Node mode below. No migration, decommissioning, listener edit or runner refactor is implied by adding this section. ### 9.1 Capability and proposed Issue #3 request The Issue #3 terminal SHALL additionally support selecting a registered \`workspaces/RuntimeConfig//runtrigger.json\` template, validating a caller-populated \`set\`, committing a run-specific trigger, executing its Node.js program with one named-arguments JSON object, and publishing a source-correlated execution receipt. The two available template-backed functions SHALL remain accessible: create/replace an Issue comment, and replace an Issue body. The proposed unambiguous Issue #3 envelope is: \`\`\`json { "runOn": "node", "forWhom": "GPT6_0000000007-example-Terminals", "runpath": "issue-comment-writer", "set": { "jsPath": "workspaces/RuntimeConfig/issue-comment-writer/issue-comment-writer.js", "args": { "issuePath": "BestNameYet/Terminals/issues/4", "commentId": "new", "jsonArrayPath": "[{\"html\":\"

example

\"}]" } } } \`\`\` The \`runOn="node"\` discriminator and this combined envelope are **design decisions proposed by this SRS**, not current supported Issue #3 syntax. For \`node\` mode, \`forWhom\`, \`runpath\`, and \`set\` SHALL be required and \`whatPrompt\` SHALL be forbidden. Existing \`$\` and \`gh\` envelopes and their semantics SHALL be preserved. No silent translation from an Issue #10-shaped body is permitted. A future implementation SHALL define and enforce mode-specific top-level schemas. ### 9.2 Requirements to incorporate (all DESIGN) | ID | Requirement | |---|---| | I3-X-001 | Extend Issue #3 command selection with a distinct \`node\` mode and preserve existing \`$\`/\`gh\` inputs and behavior unchanged. | | I3-X-002 | For Node mode, require exactly \`runOn\`, \`forWhom\`, \`runpath\`, \`set\`; reject unknown, missing, mixed-mode, ambiguous or malformed fields. | | I3-X-003 | Run Node mode only for an owner-authored, newly created Issue #3 comment; do not execute a Node command on an edit or on a PR comment. Preserve the existing create/edit behavior for shell/gh modes. | | I3-X-004 | Check owner type \`User\` and matching author ID/login before the Node execution job checks out the repository; repeat the owner verification after checkout. Avoid execution through unauthenticated or unregistered alternative paths. | | I3-X-005 | Resolve \`runpath\` as an existing *proper subfolder* under \`workspaces/RuntimeConfig/\`; accept a relative subfolder or repository-prefixed path; reject absolute, \`..\` traversal, nonexistent folders, symlink escapes and any template not a regular \`runtrigger.json\` in the selected folder. | | I3-X-006 | Read the selected template and require a nonempty \`set\` with exactly every key other than \`metadata\`, recursively matching object keys, array lengths and leaf types; reject extra or missing keys, empty collections, nulls and blank strings. A template null leaf may accept a populated scalar as in the Issue #10 implementation. | | I3-X-007 | Retain template \`metadata\` unchanged; do not permit callers to set it. Populate other template fields, preserve the original template, and create the clone exclusively with a unique name correlated to its Issue #3 source comment and creation time. | | I3-X-008 | Use the actual RuntimeConfig runner keys \`jsPath\` and \`args\` (not the obsolete prose spelling \`js_path\`); validate \`jsPath\` resolves to a file and \`args\` is a JSON object. | | I3-X-009 | Run \`node workspaces/RuntimeConfig/runner.js \`; execute the selected script as \`node JSON.stringify(args)\`; propagate child nonzero status, errors and signals. Do not imply stricter script-path isolation than the implementation actually enforces. | | I3-X-010 | Before invoking the selected program, commit and push the clone to the default branch and verify remote bytes; if publication or readback fails, do not execute the program. Record the published trigger commit. | | I3-X-011 | Preserve the source Issue #3 number, source comment ID, \`forWhom\`, mode, source event, trigger path, published commit, Actions run ID/attempt and program exit status in a machine-readable, correlated execution receipt. | | I3-X-012 | Capture program stdout/stderr or combined execution log; include log SHA-256, outcome and program exit code in the receipt; upload the trigger, log and receipt as run-correlated Actions artifacts, including when the program fails. Do not assert an artifact exists when failure occurred before its creation. | | I3-X-013 | Distinguish validation rejection, trigger persistence failure, execution failure, receipt/artifact failure and user-task outcome; command dispatch, workflow success and receipt creation alone SHALL NOT certify the user-requested target state. | | I3-X-014 | Define an explicit bounded total job timeout and serialization/concurrency key for state-mutating Node commands; never claim FIFO behavior across all Issue #3 modes without implementing it. | | I3-X-015 | Supply the selected program with documented credentials (\`GH_TOKEN\` and optional \`WORKSPACE_API\` where configured), subject to actual repository permissions; avoid disclosing secrets in saved logs, source comments or receipts. | | I3-X-016 | Keep the existing Issue #10 listener operational until a separately approved migration/deprecation; source-issue-specific clone names and receipts must never mislabel Issue #3 commands as Issue #10 commands. | | I3-X-017 | For \`issue-comment-writer\`, accept \`args={issuePath,commentId,jsonArrayPath}\`; \`issuePath\` is \`owner/repo/issues/N\` or GitHub Issue URL; \`commentId="new"\` creates, while a positive decimal ID replaces the *entire body* of a verified comment belonging to that issue. | | I3-X-018 | For \`issue-body-writer\`, accept \`args={issuePath,jsonArrayPath}\` and replace the *entire* target Issue body by PATCH; require the GitHub response body to match the submitted body. | | I3-X-019 | For both writer functions, interpret \`jsonArrayPath\` as either a repository-readable path to a JSON array or a literal serialized JSON array; require a nonempty array of nonempty objects with string values, concatenate values in their iteration order using two newline separators, and reject invalid or empty rendered output. | | I3-X-020 | Expose writer response identity (URL and comment ID or Issue number) and independently retrieve the target after mutation to verify complete expected content; appending requires first retrieving the existing body and deliberately including it in the replacement. | | I3-X-021 | Preserve per-mode error and completion semantics: Bash stdout persistence must not be conflated with Node trigger/receipt persistence; use correlation fields to identify which artifacts establish which result. | | I3-X-022 | Define an explicit idempotency/retry rule for state-mutating Issue writers so replays, duplicate events or failed post-write verification cannot silently create extra comments or overwrite an unintended body. | ### 9.3 Verification matrix for incorporated functions | ID | Test | Expected evidence | |---|---|---| | I3-XT-001 | Valid new owner Issue #3 Node command for each available RuntimeConfig template | Correct route, clone, commit/readback, Node invocation, receipt and verified side effect | | I3-XT-002 | Shell/gh regression suite after adding Node mode | Existing create/edit behavior, command schema, stdout format and exit semantics unchanged | | I3-XT-003 | Edit of existing Node-mode comment; non-owner event; PR event | No Node program execution; owner gate enforced before Node checkout | | I3-XT-004 | Missing/extra \`set\` keys, wrong nested types or array lengths, blank/null values, caller-supplied metadata | Rejected before clone publication or execution | | I3-XT-005 | Traversal/absolute/symlinked/missing folder, missing template or invalid \`jsPath\` | Safe rejection; program not executed | | I3-XT-006 | Push conflict, failed commit or remote byte mismatch | Program not invoked; failure recorded, no false persistence claim | | I3-XT-007 | Program returns nonzero, throws or is terminated; no stdout | Status and log/receipt faithfully distinguish outcomes | | I3-XT-008 | Create a new Issue comment via writer | Exactly one new comment; ID and body independently verified | | I3-XT-009 | Update an existing comment via writer; mismatched Issue/comment pair | Full replacement of correct target, or rejection before mutation | | I3-XT-010 | Replace Issue body via writer | Exact expected body after independent readback; prior body not silently appended | | I3-XT-011 | Literal and file-based array with multiple string-valued object entries | Deterministic concatenation, order and double-newline separators | | I3-XT-012 | Duplicate event/retry after a writer mutation | Defined no-duplicate/no-unintended-overwrite behavior and correlated status | | I3-XT-013 | Two concurrent Node commands and interaction with shell/gh mode | Documented per-mode ordering, isolation, artifact correlation and no unsupported FIFO claim | | I3-XT-014 | Run under Issue #3 while Issue #10 remains active | Source-issue-specific paths/receipts; no accidental Issue #10 invocation or regression | | I3-XT-015 | Program succeeds but requested task's final state is incorrect | Receipt reports program execution result while task remains unverified/failed | ### 9.4 Migration boundaries and open decisions The source Issue #10 system currently uses \`issue_comment(created)\`, an owner-gated dedicated job, per-Issue serialization, a \`runtrigger__issue10_.json\` clone, commit-before-execute, the \`jsPath\`/\`args\` runner, a \`terminals.runtimeconfig.execution-receipt.v1\` receipt and a 30-day Actions artifact. Those are evidence for the required capabilities, not proof of their presence in Issue #3. Pending design decisions include: whether Node-mode invocation should use the proposed \`runOn="node"\` envelope or a differently named discriminator; whether Node comment edits must be ignored at the routing layer or rejected downstream; whether per-mode serialization should be global or scoped to the target Issue; whether receipt durability must exceed the artifact retention period; and whether replays may be safely deduplicated using source comment ID and run attempt. All choices must be resolved before marking the SRS accepted. ","readmeNote":" ## Issue #10 capability incorporation (proposed) [SRS.md](SRS.md#9-incorporating-issue-10-runtimeconfig-capabilities-into-issue-3-design) now specifies the proposed addition of Issue #10's generic RuntimeConfig Node.js execution and the Issue-comment/body writer functions to the Issue #3 terminal. Requirements I3-X-001 through I3-X-022 and tests I3-XT-001 through I3-XT-015 cover mode selection, authorization, exact template validation, commit-before-execution, receipts, side effects, regression, concurrency and failure semantics. This is a design addition only: the working Issue #3 interface still accepts only Bash and GitHub CLI, and Issue #10 remains active. ","sourcesNote":" ## Issue #10 capability sources for proposed Issue #3 integration - [Issue #10 instructions](https://github.com/BestNameYet/Terminals/issues/10): existing Node command contract and trigger lifecycle; note that its prose uses the stale \`js_path\` spelling. - [Issue #10 execution workflow](../../.github/workflows/issue-10-runtimeconfig.yml): owner checks, regression gate, clone commit/push/readback, serialized Node run, execution receipt and artifact. - [RuntimeConfig trigger validator](../RuntimeConfig/prepare-runtrigger.js): exact \`runpath\`/\`set\` and type/path validation; currently hardcodes Issue #10 source identity and clone name. - [RuntimeConfig Node runner](../RuntimeConfig/runner.js): authoritative camelCase \`jsPath\`, \`args\` and child exit propagation. - [Issue comment writer](../RuntimeConfig/issue-comment-writer/issue-comment-writer.js) and [template](../RuntimeConfig/issue-comment-writer/runtrigger.json): create/replace Issue comments and input contract. - [Issue body writer](../RuntimeConfig/issue-body-writer/issue-body-writer.js) and [template](../RuntimeConfig/issue-body-writer/runtrigger.json): replace Issue body and input contract. - [RuntimeConfig regression tests](../RuntimeConfig/prepare-runtrigger.test.js): parser, clone, authorization and runner test cases. The proposed Issue #3 Node command envelope and requirements are normative design additions; no existing Issue #3 implementation or test result is represented as satisfying them. Incorporating Issue #10 RuntimeConfig capabilities into Issue #3"); patch("README.md",blocks.readmeNote,"## Issue #10 capability incorporation (proposed)"); patch("SOURCES.md",blocks.sourcesNote,"## Issue #10 capability sources for proposed Issue #3 integration"); NODE
